subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_family:QwigleyRegular" subtitle="A 3D designer who works in air" heading_margin="margin-bottom:10px;"]What Is an Inflatable Artist?[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]An inflatable artist is responsible for the form. The work is 3D design: modelling the character, checking how it reads from a hundred metres away and from directly beneath, then breaking that shape into panels a fabricator can cut and sew. The medium has a long history in art. Ant Farm were building architectural-scale inflatables in 1970, and the form now runs from gallery pieces through to the lit night sculptures that hold a festival crowd after dark.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]Plenty of companies will manufacture an inflatable to supplied dimensions. Fewer will work out what the object should be. Oddtoe is engaged at that earlier stage, by agencies, producers and councils who bring the studio in before there is anything to quote. Closely related Oddtoe practices often end up inside the same commission: installation art and kinetic sculpture.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_config="default_row_small_paddings" dfd_row_responsive_enable="dfd-row-responsive-enable" responsive_styles="padding_left_mobile:10|padding_right_mobile:10"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="60" screen_tablet_spacer_size="50" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_family:BebasNeueRegular|letter_spacing:0" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_family:QwigleyRegular" subtitle="Characters, walk-ins, night pieces, mascots, and replicas" heading_margin="margin-bottom:10px;"]What Can Oddtoe Make?[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]Giant brand characters, walk-in environments, illuminated night pieces, wearable mascot costumes, and oversized food or product replicas. Most briefs land in one of those five, and several can be combined into one site: a character by day that lights from the inside after dark. The starting point is usually a character. Oddtoe owns a cast of them — see character design — and an existing character survives being scaled to ten metres better than a logo does.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]• Giant characters — a single figure, 4m and up
• Walk-in environments — arches, domes, tunnels people enter
• Illuminated night pieces — lit from within for after dark
• Wearable mascot costumes — roaming, crowd-facing
• Product replicas — the oversized bottle, jar, or burger The 3D model is reusable. The same asset that proves the piece to a client produces pitch renders, animated content for screens or projection, and social cutdowns. Related studio practices: props and fabrication and topiary and planted forms.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_responsive_enable="dfd-row-responsive-enable" responsive_styles="padding_left_mobile:10|padding_right_mobile:10"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="60" screen_tablet_spacer_size="50" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_family:BebasNeueRegular|letter_spacing:0" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_family:QwigleyRegular" subtitle="Which one is your brief?" heading_margin="margin-bottom:10px;"]Inflatable Art, Advertising Inflatable, or Walk-In Structure?[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/6"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="2/3"][vc_column_text css=""]Three things get ordered using the same word. This table sets out what each one is, where it goes, and what Oddtoe hands over.

What Oddtoe deliversConcept, character, patterns, fabrication, installConcept, artwork, fabrication, install, runConcept, layout, fabrication, install, run
[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/6"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="60" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_config="default_row_small_paddings" anchor="who" dfd_row_responsive_enable="dfd-row-responsive-enable" responsive_styles="padding_left_mobile:10|padding_right_mobile:10"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="60" screen_tablet_spacer_size="50" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_family:BebasNeueRegular|letter_spacing:0" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_family:QwigleyRegular" subtitle="Brands, festivals, councils, and shopping centres" heading_margin="margin-bottom:10px;"]Who Commissions Large-Scale Inflatables?[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]Marketing and activation agencies, festivals and event producers, local councils, shopping centres, and museums doing placemaking work. Each wants a different outcome from the same object, and the design changes accordingly. Australia’s event promotion and management industry is worth $13.1 billion in 2026, according to IBISWorld. Inflatables sit inside that spend as the hero object — the thing on site that is visible from the car park.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]Agencies and brands commission a character or a product replica as the centrepiece of an activation. See experiential marketing and the agency list. Festivals and event producers commission night pieces and walk-in structures that hold a crowd in one part of the site. Councils and placemaking teams commission seasonal pieces that draw foot traffic into a precinct and pack away afterwards. Shopping centres and retail commission the returning seasonal install, photographed by every family who walks past it.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_config="default_row_small_paddings" anchor="how" dfd_row_responsive_enable="dfd-row-responsive-enable" responsive_styles="padding_left_mobile:10|padding_right_mobile:10"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="60" screen_tablet_spacer_size="50" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_family:BebasNeueRegular|letter_spacing:0" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_family:QwigleyRegular" subtitle="Designed in 3D, built by specialists, planned around the site" heading_margin="margin-bottom:10px;"]How Does an Oddtoe Inflatable Get Made?[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]Six steps: brief and site, character and concept in 3D, pattern and engineering, fabrication, test inflate, then install and run. Design sits with the studio; fabrication goes to a specialist inflatable maker. 1. Brief and site. Footprint, anchor points or ballast, overhead clearance, wind exposure, blower power, and how long the piece has to stand. 2. Character and concept. Modelled in 3D so the piece can be seen at true scale in the actual space before any fabric is cut. Early exploration uses generative AI; the drawings a fabricator works from are drawn properly.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]3. Pattern and engineering. The form is broken into panels, seams are placed where they will not distort the shape, and blower sizing, internal baffling and anchor points are specified. 4. Fabrication. Built by a specialist inflatable maker. Material and test documentation are specified here against the venue’s own rules, because an open field and a shopping centre ask for different paperwork. 5. Test inflate. Fully inflated and photographed at the factory before it ships. 6. Install and run. Anchored and ballasted on the agreed day, to a wind management plan that sets the speed at which the piece comes down.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_config="default_row_small_paddings" anchor="words" dfd_row_responsive_enable="dfd-row-responsive-enable" responsive_styles="padding_left_mobile:10|padding_right_mobile:10"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="60" screen_tablet_spacer_size="50" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_family:BebasNeueRegular|letter_spacing:0" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_family:QwigleyRegular" subtitle="The thing people stand under and photograph" heading_margin="margin-bottom:10px;"]Why Oddtoe Makes Inflatables[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]A giant inflatable is built to be photographed. Someone walking past has to stop, look up, and want a picture of themselves underneath it. Everything else about the piece follows from that. Most of them fail at it because they start from a logo. A logo at ten metres is still a logo. A character at ten metres reads as somebody who has turned up.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]So the design covers the moment as well as the object: where a person stands, what is behind them in the frame, and what the thing appears to be doing while they are there. A figure that leans out over a crowd or reaches down gives people a position to take up. A smooth branded shape gives them nothing to work with. Giant inflatables?

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_accordion style="style-3" active_section="1" font_size="18" tab_title_google_fonts="yes" tab_title_custom_fonts="font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic|font_style:700%20bold%20regular%3A700%3Anormal" icon_size="18" icon_color="#000000" active_two_px_border="on"][vc_tta_section i_icon_fontawesome="fas fa-wind" add_icon="true" title="What is an inflatable artist?" tab_id="1756100000001-inflatable-artist-faq-1"][vc_column_text css=""]

An inflatable artist works out what the object should be and how it holds its shape. It is 3D design work: modelling the character, testing how it reads from a hundred metres away and from directly underneath, then breaking that shape into panels a fabricator can cut and sew. Oddtoe designs the piece and hands over a finished pattern set.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section i_icon_fontawesome="fas fa-cube" add_icon="true" title="Can Oddtoe design an inflatable if someone else is manufacturing it?" tab_id="1756100000002-inflatable-artist-faq-2"][vc_column_text css=""]

Yes, and agencies with an existing factory relationship often work this way. Oddtoe develops the character and the 3D model, produces the client-facing renders, and delivers a pattern set your own fabricator can build from. On that arrangement Oddtoe is the design resource on the job and your factory stays the supplier.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section i_icon_fontawesome="fas fa-dollar-sign" add_icon="true" title="How much does a giant custom inflatable cost?" tab_id="1756100000003-inflatable-artist-faq-3"][vc_column_text css=""]

Cost is driven by height, how many separate panels the shape needs, whether it is lit from inside, whether the public can enter it, and how long it stays up. A single figure and a walk-in tunnel with lighting are very different budgets. Oddtoe quotes each brief individually — send the site, the dates, and a rough height.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section i_icon_fontawesome="fas fa-expand-arrows-alt" add_icon="true" title="How big can a large-scale inflatable be?" tab_id="1756100000004-inflatable-artist-faq-4"][vc_column_text css=""]

Custom display inflatables are commonly made from about 4 metres up to 20 metres tall, and walk-in structures spread further across the ground than they rise. The limit is usually set by the site: available anchor points, wind exposure, overhead clearance, and how much ballast can physically be brought in.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section i_icon_fontawesome="far fa-clock" add_icon="true" title="How long does it take to design and make one?" tab_id="1756100000005-inflatable-artist-faq-5"][vc_column_text css=""]

Allow four to eight weeks. Design and pattern work take one to two weeks, fabrication two to three, and freight the rest. Rush builds are possible when the shape is simple. Booking the fabrication slot early is what protects the date.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section i_icon_fontawesome="fas fa-clipboard-check" add_icon="true" title="What approvals, engineering and insurance do giant inflatables need in Australia?" tab_id="1756100000006-inflatable-artist-faq-6"][vc_column_text css=""]

It depends on the venue and on whether the public can enter the piece. Expect to be asked for an engineering design certificate covering hold-down ballast and a maximum design wind speed as a three-second gust under AS/NZS 1170.2, a wind management plan, and public liability cover. Indoor and shopping-centre sites also want fire-retardant test evidence against AS 1530.3. Anything the public enters or bounces on counts as an amusement device under AS 3533.4.1, which is a heavier regime again. Oddtoe works out which of these a site triggers during design, so the build is specified to suit the site from the start.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section i_icon_fontawesome="fas fa-sync-alt" add_icon="true" title="Can an inflatable be reused at another event?" tab_id="1756100000007-inflatable-artist-faq-7"][vc_column_text css=""]

Usually. A giant inflatable packs into crates, travels as freight, and goes back up at the next site with the same blowers. Seasonal pieces are common — the same character returns each year and stores flat in between.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section i_icon_fontawesome="fas fa-map-marker-alt" add_icon="true" title="Where is Oddtoe based, and can you deliver internationally?" tab_id="1756100000008-inflatable-artist-faq-8"][vc_column_text css=""]

Oddtoe designs from Melbourne, Australia, and finished pieces ship worldwide direct from the fabricator, so the studio's location does not limit where a piece can stand. Installation is a separate decision: plenty of clients use their own local crew, and where you would rather Oddtoe ran the install, travel and time are quoted up front.

[vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][vc_column_text css=””]Oddtoe is an experiential design and generative-AI animation studio based in Melbourne, creating projection, installation, and animated work for events, venues, and galleries. A 3D designer who works in air

What Is an Inflatable Artist?

[vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][vc_column_text css=””]An inflatable artist is responsible for the form. The work is 3D design: modelling the character, checking how it reads from a hundred metres away and from directly beneath, then breaking that shape into panels a fabricator can cut and sew.

The medium has a long history in art. Ant Farm were building architectural-scale inflatables in 1970, and the form now runs from gallery pieces through to the lit night sculptures that hold a festival crowd after dark.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][vc_column_text css=””]Plenty of companies will manufacture an inflatable to supplied dimensions. Fewer will work out what the object should be. Oddtoe is engaged at that earlier stage, by agencies, producers and councils who bring the studio in before there is anything to quote.

Closely related Oddtoe practices often end up inside the same commission: installation art and kinetic sculpture.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner]

[/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check=”row-background-dark” dfd_enable_overlay=”” dfd_row_config=”default_row_small_paddings” dfd_row_responsive_enable=”dfd-row-responsive-enable” responsive_styles=”padding_left_mobile:10|padding_right_mobile:10″][vc_column]

What Can Oddtoe Make?

[vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][vc_column_text css=””]Giant brand characters, walk-in environments, illuminated night pieces, wearable mascot costumes, and oversized food or product replicas. Most briefs land in one of those five, and several can be combined into one site: a character by day that lights from the inside after dark.

The starting point is usually a character. Oddtoe owns a cast of them — see character design — and an existing character survives being scaled to ten metres better than a logo does.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][vc_column_text css=””]• Giant characters — a single figure, 4m and up
• Walk-in environments — arches, domes, tunnels people enter
• Illuminated night pieces — lit from within for after dark
• Wearable mascot costumes — roaming, crowd-facing
• Product replicas — the oversized bottle, jar, or burger

The 3D model is reusable. The same asset that proves the piece to a client produces pitch renders, animated content for screens or projection, and social cutdowns. Related studio practices: props and fabrication and topiary and planted forms.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner]

[vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/6″][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”2/3″][vc_column_text css=””]Three things get ordered using the same word. This table sets out what each one is, where it goes, and what Oddtoe hands over.

Who Commissions Large-Scale Inflatables?

[vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][vc_column_text css=””]Marketing and activation agencies, festivals and event producers, local councils, shopping centres, and museums doing placemaking work. Each wants a different outcome from the same object, and the design changes accordingly.

Australia’s event promotion and management industry is worth $13.1 billion in 2026, according to IBISWorld. Inflatables sit inside that spend as the hero object — the thing on site that is visible from the car park.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][vc_column_text css=””]Agencies and brands commission a character or a product replica as the centrepiece of an activation. See experiential marketing and the agency list.

Festivals and event producers commission night pieces and walk-in structures that hold a crowd in one part of the site.

Councils and placemaking teams commission seasonal pieces that draw foot traffic into a precinct and pack away afterwards.

Shopping centres and retail commission the returning seasonal install, photographed by every family who walks past it.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner]

[/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check=”row-background-dark” dfd_enable_overlay=”” dfd_row_config=”default_row_small_paddings” anchor=”how” dfd_row_responsive_enable=”dfd-row-responsive-enable” responsive_styles=”padding_left_mobile:10|padding_right_mobile:10″][vc_column]

Designed in 3D, built by specialists, planned around the site

How Does an Oddtoe Inflatable Get Made?

[vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][vc_column_text css=””]Six steps: brief and site, character and concept in 3D, pattern and engineering, fabrication, test inflate, then install and run. Design sits with the studio; fabrication goes to a specialist inflatable maker.

1. Brief and site. Footprint, anchor points or ballast, overhead clearance, wind exposure, blower power, and how long the piece has to stand.

2. Character and concept. Modelled in 3D so the piece can be seen at true scale in the actual space before any fabric is cut. Early exploration uses generative AI; the drawings a fabricator works from are drawn properly.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][vc_column_text css=””]3. Pattern and engineering. The form is broken into panels, seams are placed where they will not distort the shape, and blower sizing, internal baffling and anchor points are specified.

4. Fabrication. Built by a specialist inflatable maker. Material and test documentation are specified here against the venue’s own rules, because an open field and a shopping centre ask for different paperwork.

5. Test inflate. Fully inflated and photographed at the factory before it ships.

6. Install and run. Anchored and ballasted on the agreed day, to a wind management plan that sets the speed at which the piece comes down.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner]

[/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check=”row-background-dark” dfd_enable_overlay=”” dfd_row_config=”default_row_small_paddings” anchor=”words” dfd_row_responsive_enable=”dfd-row-responsive-enable” responsive_styles=”padding_left_mobile:10|padding_right_mobile:10″][vc_column]

The thing people stand under and photograph

Why Oddtoe Makes Inflatables

[vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][vc_column_text css=””]A giant inflatable is built to be photographed. Someone walking past has to stop, look up, and want a picture of themselves underneath it. Everything else about the piece follows from that.

Most of them fail at it because they start from a logo. A logo at ten metres is still a logo. A character at ten metres reads as somebody who has turned up.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][vc_column_text css=””]So the design covers the moment as well as the object: where a person stands, what is behind them in the frame, and what the thing appears to be doing while they are there. A figure that leans out over a crowd or reaches down gives people a position to take up. A smooth branded shape gives them nothing to work with.

Questions about

Giant inflatables?

[/vc_column_text]

[dfd_accordion style=”style-3″ active_section=”1″ font_size=”18″ tab_title_google_fonts=”yes” tab_title_custom_fonts=”font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic|font_style:700%20bold%20regular%3A700%3Anormal” icon_size=”18″ icon_color=”#000000″ active_two_px_border=”on”][vc_tta_section i_icon_fontawesome=”fas fa-wind” add_icon=”true” title=”What is an inflatable artist?” tab_id=”1756100000001-inflatable-artist-faq-1″][vc_column_text css=””]

An inflatable artist works out what the object should be and how it holds its shape. It is 3D design work: modelling the character, testing how it reads from a hundred metres away and from directly underneath, then breaking that shape into panels a fabricator can cut and sew. Oddtoe designs the piece and hands over a finished pattern set.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section i_icon_fontawesome=”fas fa-cube” add_icon=”true” title=”Can Oddtoe design an inflatable if someone else is manufacturing it?” tab_id=”1756100000002-inflatable-artist-faq-2″][vc_column_text css=””]

Yes, and agencies with an existing factory relationship often work this way. Oddtoe develops the character and the 3D model, produces the client-facing renders, and delivers a pattern set your own fabricator can build from. On that arrangement Oddtoe is the design resource on the job and your factory stays the supplier.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section i_icon_fontawesome=”fas fa-dollar-sign” add_icon=”true” title=”How much does a giant custom inflatable cost?” tab_id=”1756100000003-inflatable-artist-faq-3″][vc_column_text css=””]

Cost is driven by height, how many separate panels the shape needs, whether it is lit from inside, whether the public can enter it, and how long it stays up. A single figure and a walk-in tunnel with lighting are very different budgets. Oddtoe quotes each brief individually — send the site, the dates, and a rough height.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section i_icon_fontawesome=”fas fa-expand-arrows-alt” add_icon=”true” title=”How big can a large-scale inflatable be?” tab_id=”1756100000004-inflatable-artist-faq-4″][vc_column_text css=””]

Custom display inflatables are commonly made from about 4 metres up to 20 metres tall, and walk-in structures spread further across the ground than they rise. The limit is usually set by the site: available anchor points, wind exposure, overhead clearance, and how much ballast can physically be brought in.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section i_icon_fontawesome=”far fa-clock” add_icon=”true” title=”How long does it take to design and make one?” tab_id=”1756100000005-inflatable-artist-faq-5″][vc_column_text css=””]

Allow four to eight weeks. Design and pattern work take one to two weeks, fabrication two to three, and freight the rest. Rush builds are possible when the shape is simple. Booking the fabrication slot early is what protects the date.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section i_icon_fontawesome=”fas fa-clipboard-check” add_icon=”true” title=”What approvals, engineering and insurance do giant inflatables need in Australia?” tab_id=”1756100000006-inflatable-artist-faq-6″][vc_column_text css=””]

It depends on the venue and on whether the public can enter the piece. Expect to be asked for an engineering design certificate covering hold-down ballast and a maximum design wind speed as a three-second gust under AS/NZS 1170.2, a wind management plan, and public liability cover. Indoor and shopping-centre sites also want fire-retardant test evidence against AS 1530.3. Anything the public enters or bounces on counts as an amusement device under AS 3533.4.1, which is a heavier regime again. Oddtoe works out which of these a site triggers during design, so the build is specified to suit the site from the start.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section i_icon_fontawesome=”fas fa-sync-alt” add_icon=”true” title=”Can an inflatable be reused at another event?” tab_id=”1756100000007-inflatable-artist-faq-7″][vc_column_text css=””]

Usually. A giant inflatable packs into crates, travels as freight, and goes back up at the next site with the same blowers. Seasonal pieces are common — the same character returns each year and stores flat in between.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section i_icon_fontawesome=”fas fa-map-marker-alt” add_icon=”true” title=”Where is Oddtoe based, and can you deliver internationally?” tab_id=”1756100000008-inflatable-artist-faq-8″][vc_column_text css=””]

Oddtoe designs from Melbourne, Australia, and finished pieces ship worldwide direct from the fabricator, so the studio’s location does not limit where a piece can stand. Installation is a separate decision: plenty of clients use their own local crew, and where you would rather Oddtoe ran the install, travel and time are quoted up front.
